contradictions.what: Rep says IT was fine with it, then reveals the IT lead was nervous about moving before spring and conditional on finance approval.
Rep says we lost on price, then concedes it may not be only the rate, then says the rate killed it.
Rep says nothing bombed and it was a good cycle, but Lucy asked for a business case for Martin and we had none.
The CFO's words are quoted two ways: 'he's not going to pay more for the same thing' and 'Why would I pay more for the same thing.'
Rep says the offers are not the same thing, yet Martin got only a rate comparison and nothing from us on value.
Rep says value analysis wasn't needed because Lucy was sold, but the CFO decided with nothing from us and the champion asked for help.
Champion called approval a formality, but the CFO, whom we never met, said no.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Said 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed' and moved to 'we lost on price'. Later turns show an unmet business-case request.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get? A figure for Fernbrook.
dodges.what: First answered with the generic uplift slide and 'Lucy got it'. Admitted no customer-specific figure only after being pressed.

dodges.question: What did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Paused, answered 'Nothing from us', then assumed Lucy told him.

dodges.question: If we had matched the price, would we have won? What else would have needed to be true?
dodges.what: Said 'Yes. Probably', then listed other blockers, then fell back to 'the rate is what killed it'.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Described sending the deck and pricing proposal rather than saying we had no business case.
